# Import libraries and set up environment

Similar to the previous notebook, we will set up parameters and directories.
First we define whether to include MN2 data.

```{r}
#| label: eval_mn2

eval_mn2 <- TRUE

if (!eval_mn2) {
  cat("MN2 data will not be included in the analysis.")
} else {
  cat("MN2 data will be included in the analysis.")
}
```

Then we set up the output path.
```{r}
#| label: output-path-setup

src_dir <- "../../src/"
output_dir_root <- "../../output_figures/"

if (!dir.exists(output_dir_root)) {
  stop(paste0("Root of output directory does not exist: ", output_dir_root))
}

if (!eval_mn2) {
  output_dir <- paste0(output_dir_root, "batch2_differential_expression/")
} else {
  output_dir <- paste0(
    output_dir_root,
    "batch2_differential_expression_including_MN2/"
  )
}

diff_expression_dir <- paste0(output_dir, "differential_expression/")
dir.create(diff_expression_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

Additionally, we source the same helper functions as before.
```{r}
#| label: sourcing-cross-notebook-functions

source(paste0(src_dir, 'plotting_funcs.R'))
source(paste0(src_dir, 'msigdbr_to_leapr.R'))
```

# Differential expression analysis

For the differential expression and pathway enrichment analysis we set some parameters first.
These consist of the spheroids, agents and timepoints we want to analyze, but more importantly the thresholds for log fold change and p-value to define which proteins are considered to be differentially expressed and as a result impact the pathway enrichment analysis.

```{r}
#| label: diff-ex-params
#| 
spheroids <- as_tibble(colData(experiment)) %>% pull(spheroid) %>% unique()
agents <- c('Mirda', 'TNO155', 'Palbo', 'Vorino')
timepoints <- c("8hr", "24hr", "48hr")
log_fc <- 1
pval <- 0.1
```

With the parameters set, we can generate the differential expression plots.

```{r}
#| label: plot-diff-ex-plots

plots <- list()
plots_agents <- list()

for (spheroid in spheroids) {
  for (agent in agents) {
    for (timepoint in timepoints) {
      experiment_subset <- experiment[,
        experiment$agent %in%
          c(agent, "DMSO") &
          experiment$timepoint == timepoint
      ]

      plots[[spheroid]][[agent]][[timepoint]] <- plot_diff_ex(
        experiment_subset,
        agent,
        timepoint,
        log_fc = log_fc,
        pval = pval,
        prot_type = 'global',
        spheroid = spheroid
      )
      plot_title <- paste(
        spheroid,
        'global proteomics:',
        agent,
        "vs. Control"
      )
    }
    plots_agents[[spheroid]][[agent]] <- plot_diff_ex_grid(
      plots[[spheroid]][[agent]],
      plot_title
    )
    print(plots_agents[[spheroid]][[agent]])
  }
}
```

And as always we will save the plots to files in the output directory.

```{r}
#| label: save-diff-ex-plots

agents <- c('Mirda', 'TNO155', 'Palbo', 'Vorino')
for (agent in agents) {
  for (spheroid in spheroids) {
    fname <- paste0(
      diff_expression_dir,
      "batch2_diff-ex_",
      "global-proteomics_",
      agent,
      "_",
      spheroid,
      ".pdf"
    )
    ggsave(
      fname,
      plot = plots_agents[[spheroid]][[agent]],
      height = 5,
      width = 7
    )
  }
}
```

# Pathway enrichment analysis

Now we take the "most interesting" results from the differential expression analysis and perform pathway enrichment analysis on it. This will allow us to identify any biological pathways that are significantly enriched in the differentially expressed proteins, which can provide insights into the underlying biological processes affected by the treatments.

## Data preparation

As a first step we will generate the differential expression results for all agents and timepoints, and store them in a list for downstream analysis. We will use the `calc_diff_ex` function to calculate the differential expression results, which takes in a `SummarizedExperiment` object, the names of the two groups to compare, and various parameters for filtering and adjusting the results.

Since we are dealing only with drugs (agents) that have a DMSO control, we will use DMSO as the control group for all comparisons. We will also set the `align_by` parameter to `"Protein.Group"`, which is the unified protein identifier used in the global proteomics data.

One important note to make is that we will use `leapR` to perform the pathway enrichment analysis later. In the current evaluation, `leapR` accepts only one column to filter by to generate a list of "targets" (i.e. differentially expressed proteins) that are compared against the background protein abundance to generate enriched pathways. Note that we define differentally expressed proteins both by their *adjusted p-value* and their *log fold change*, as caluculated by `limma`. Filtering by only one of these columns will not yield the results we are after. Furthermore, we want to distinguish between enriched and depleted pathways (i.e. "up" and "down regulated" pathways) after drug treatment. To enable us to make this distinction and capture both aspects, we will create a signed p-value column. This is done with the helper function `sgn_pval` defined below.

```{r}
#| label: sgn-pval-helper-function
sgn_pval <- function(diff_ex) {
  row_dat <- rowData(diff_ex)
  row_dat$sgn.adj.P.Val <- sign(row_dat$logFC) * (1 - row_dat$adj.P.Val)
  rowData(diff_ex) <- row_dat
  diff_ex
}
```

With this helper function defined we can now calculate the differential expression results with the signed p-value included.

```{r}
#| label: calc-diff-ex-for-pathway-enrichment

all_diff_ex <- list()
ctrl <- "DMSO"

for (spheroid in spheroids) {
  for (agent in agents) {
    for (timepoint in timepoints) {
      experiment_subset <- experiment[,
        experiment$agent %in%
          c(agent, ctrl) &
          experiment$timepoint == timepoint
      ]

      group_1 <- paste0(spheroid, "_", timepoint, "_", ctrl)
      group_2 <- paste0(spheroid, "_", timepoint, "_", agent)

      diff_ex <- calc_diff_ex(
        experiment_subset,
        group_1,
        group_2,
        align_by = "Protein.Group"
      ) %>%
        sgn_pval(.) # adding a signed pval column for enrichment_in_sets

      all_diff_ex[[spheroid]][[agent]][[timepoint]] <- diff_ex
    }
  }
}
```

## Pathway enrichment plots
Now we can perform the run the pathway enrichment analysis. 

But first we need to load the necessary data for the pathway enrichment analysis. We will use the `ncipid` and `krbpaths` datasets from the `leapR` package, which contain information about pathways and their associated proteins.

```{r}
#| label: load-pathway-enrichment-data
data("ncipid")
data("krbpaths")
msigdb_pid <- get_genesets_from_msigdb(
  species = "Homo sapiens",
  msigdb_subcollection = "CP:PID"
)
```

We will also set up some global parmeters for the pathway enrichment analysis, including the log fold change and p-value cutoffs for selecting differentially expressed proteins.

```{r}
#| label: pathway-enrichment-parameters
geneset <- msigdb_pid
id_column <- "Genes"
```

First we will generate all of the pathway enrichments for each combination of spheroid, agent, and timepoint. This will serve as the basis for additional analysis.

```{r}
all_enriched_pathways <- list()

for (spheroid in spheroids) {
  for (agent in agents) {
    for (timepoint in timepoints) {
      tryCatch(
        {
          enriched_pathways <- leapR(
            geneset = geneset,
            eset = all_diff_ex[[spheroid]][[agent]][[timepoint]],
            enrichment_method = "enrichment_in_sets",
            assay_name = 'proteomics',
            id_column = id_column,
            primary_columns = "sgn.adj.P.Val",
            threshold = 1 - pval,
            greaterthan = TRUE
          )
          all_enriched_pathways[[spheroid]][[agent]][[
            timepoint
          ]] <- enriched_pathways
        },
        error = function(msg) {
          message(
            paste0(
              "pval of '",
              pval,
              "' did not result in differentially expressed proteins for agent '",
              agent,
              "' at timepoint '",
              timepoint,
              "' in spheroid '",
              spheroid,
              "'"
            )
          )
          return(NA)
        }
      )
    }
  }
}
```

Now we can repeat that for the depleted pathways as well.

```{r}
all_depleted_pathways <- list()
for (spheroid in spheroids) {
  for (agent in agents) {
    for (timepoint in timepoints) {
      tryCatch(
        {
          depleted_pathways <- leapR(
            geneset = geneset,
            eset = all_diff_ex[[spheroid]][[agent]][[timepoint]],
            enrichment_method = "enrichment_in_sets",
            assay_name = 'proteomics',
            id_column = id_column,
            primary_columns = "sgn.adj.P.Val",
            threshold = -(1 - pval),
            greaterthan = FALSE
          )
          all_depleted_pathways[[spheroid]][[agent]][[
            timepoint
          ]] <- depleted_pathways
        },
        error = function(msg) {
          message(
            paste0(
              "pval of '",
              pval,
              "' did not result in differentially expressed proteins for agent '",
              agent,
              "' at timepoint '",
              timepoint,
              "'"
            )
          )
          return(NA)
        }
      )
    }
  }
}
```

## Visualizing the number of significantly enriched pathways across spheroids, agents and timepoints

Here we will visualize the number of significantly enriched pathways across spheroids, agents and timepoints. We will first gather the significantly enriched pathways into a single data frame, and then generate a bar plot showing the number of significantly enriched pathways for each spheroid, agent and timepoint.

The code cell below gathers the significantly enriched pathways into a single data frame, and filters for pathways with a BH adjusted p-value less than 0.05.
```{r}
#| label: gather-sig-pathways

filter_pathways <- function(
  df,
  label,
  filter_col = "BH_pvalue",
  threshold = 0.05,
  larger_than = FALSE
) {
  df_ret <- df %>%
    rownames_to_column(., var = "pathway") %>%
    as_tibble(.) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(!!sym(filter_col)) %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      if (larger_than) {
        !!sym(filter_col) > threshold
      } else {
        !!sym(filter_col) < threshold
      }
    ) %>%
    # in some weird edge cases leapR produces good pvalues for enriched sets
    # (using enrichment_in_sets) despite that the ingroup (i.e. proteins that
    # are detected to be significantly differentially expressed and in the
    # geneset that defines a pathway) is 0. Those edge cases are filtered out
    # with the next `filter()` call
    dplyr::filter(
      ingroup_n > 0
    ) %>%
    mutate(category = label)
  if (nrow(df_ret) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  return(df_ret)
}

dfs_sig_pathways <- list()

for (spheroid in spheroids) {
  for (agent in agents) {
    for (timepoint in timepoints) {
      df_enriched <- all_enriched_pathways[[spheroid]][[agent]][[timepoint]]
      if (is.null(df_enriched)) {
        pathways_enriched <- NULL
      } else {
        pathways_enriched <- filter_pathways(df_enriched, "enriched")
      }

      df_depleted <- all_depleted_pathways[[spheroid]][[agent]][[timepoint]]
      if (is.null(df_depleted)) {
        pathways_depleted <- NULL
      } else {
        pathways_depleted <- filter_pathways(df_depleted, "depleted")
      }

      label <- paste0(
        spheroid,
        "_",
        agent,
        "_",
        timepoint
      )
      if (!is.null(pathways_enriched) & !is.null(pathways_depleted)) {
        dfs_sig_pathways[[label]] <- rbind(pathways_enriched, pathways_depleted)
      } else if (!is.null(pathways_enriched)) {
        dfs_sig_pathways[[label]] <- pathways_enriched
      } else if (!is.null(pathways_depleted)) {
        dfs_sig_pathways[[label]] <- pathways_depleted
      } else {
        next
      }
    }
  }
}

sig_pathways <- bind_rows(
  dfs_sig_pathways,
  .id = "spheroid_agent_timepoint"
) %>%
  separate(
    spheroid_agent_timepoint,
    into = c("spheroid", "agent", "timepoint"),
    sep = "_"
  ) %>%
  select(
    pathway,
    spheroid,
    agent,
    timepoint,
    category
  )
sig_pathways
```

Now we can generate a bar plot showing the number of significantly enriched pathways for each spheroid, agent and timepoint.

```{r}
#| label: plot-sig-pathway-counts
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-align: "center"
#| fig-cap: "Significant enriched pathways across spheroids, agents and timepoints."

patterns <- c(
  "JHU2202" = "none",
  "MN4" = "stripe",
  "WU225" = "crosshatch",
  "MN2" = "circle"
)

sig_pathways_grouped <- sig_pathways %>%
  group_by(spheroid, agent, timepoint, category) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  complete(spheroid, agent, timepoint, category, fill = list(count = 0)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(category = ifelse(category == "enriched", "up", "down")) %>%
  mutate(category = factor(category, levels = c("up", "down"))) %>%
  mutate(timepoint = factor(timepoint, levels = c("8hr", "24hr", "48hr"))) %>%
  mutate(count = ifelse(category == "up", count, -count))

plot_sig_pathway_counts <- ggplot(
  sig_pathways_grouped,
  aes(x = timepoint, y = count)
) +
  geom_col_pattern(
    aes(fill = agent, pattern = spheroid),
    position = position_dodge2(preserve = "single"),
    color = "black",
    pattern_color = "black",
    pattern_fill = "black",
    # pattern_size = 0.5,
    pattern_angle = 45,
    pattern_density = 0.05,
    pattern_spacing = 0.02
  ) +
  scale_pattern_manual(
    values = patterns,
    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(fill = "grey70")) # <- make lighter
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = agent_colors,
    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(pattern = "none")) # <- hide pattern
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~category, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y", strip.position = "left") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Up / down regulated pathways across spheroids, agents and timepoints",
    x = "Timepoint",
    y = "Count of up / down regulated pathways",
    fill = "Agent",
    pattern = "Spheroid"
  )
print(plot_sig_pathway_counts)
```

As we can see from the plot above, the time point with the most significantly enriched pathways is the 48hr time point, and the agent with the most significantly enriched pathways is Mirda. Specifically the fact that the 48hr timepoint has the most significantly enriched pathways is consistent with the fact that the 48hr timepoint also has the most differentially expressed proteins. 

```{r}
#| label: save-sig-pathway-counts-plot
#| eval: !expr params$saveplots
#| echo: false

ggsave(
  filename = paste0(diff_expression_dir, "batch2_sig_pathway_counts.png"),
  plot = plot_sig_pathway_counts,
  height = 6,
  width = 8
)
```

## Enriched Pathways shared across spheroids, agents and timepoints

```{r}
#| label: pathway-heatmap-plot-func
#| 
plot_pathway_enrichement_heatmap <- function(pathways, time = '48hr') {
  df_subset <- pathways %>%
    filter(timepoint == time) %>%
    mutate(
      spheroid_agent = paste0(spheroid, "_", agent)
    )

  df_plot <- df_subset %>%
    select(pathway, spheroid_agent, category) %>%
    unique() %>%
    mutate(category = ifelse(category == "enriched", 1, -1)) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = spheroid_agent,
      values_from = category,
      values_fill = 0
    ) %>%
    column_to_rownames(var = "pathway")

  annotations_cols <- df_subset %>%
    select(spheroid_agent, spheroid, agent) %>%
    unique() %>%
    column_to_rownames(var = "spheroid_agent")

  annotation_colors <- list(
    agent = agent_colors[unique(annotations_cols$agent)],
    spheroid = spheroid_colors[unique(annotations_cols$spheroid)]
  )

  plot <- pheatmap(
    mat = df_plot,
    cluster_rows = TRUE,
    cluster_cols = TRUE,
    show_rownames = TRUE,
    show_colnames = FALSE,
    annotation_col = annotations_cols,
    annotation_colors = annotation_colors,
    scale = "none",
    clustering_distance_cols = "correlation",
    color = c(
      expression_colors['down'],
      expression_colors['not significant'],
      expression_colors['up']
    ),
    breaks = c(-1.5, -0.5, 0.5, 1.5),
    legend_breaks = c(-1, 0, 1),
    legend_labels = c("Down regulated", "Non-significant", "Up regulated"),
    main = paste("Pathway Enrichment at", time)
  )
  return(plot)
}
```


## Visualizing the number of differentially expressed proteins across spheroids, agents and timepoints

Similarly to the significantly enriched pathways, we can visualize the number of differentially expressed proteins across spheroids, agents and timepoints. We will first gather the differentially expressed proteins into a single data frame, and then generate a bar plot showing the number of differentially expressed proteins for each spheroid, agent and timepoint.

The code cell below gathers the differentially expressed proteins into a single data frame, and filters for proteins with an adjusted p-value less than 0.1 and an absolute log fold change greater than 0.5. The resulting data frame contains the spheroid, agent, timepoint, protein group, protein names, genes, log fold change, and adjusted p-value for each differentially expressed protein across all spheroids, agents and timepoints, based on the enriched pathways we previously identified.

```{r}
#| label: gather-diff-ex-prots
#| 

tmp <- list()
for (spheroid in spheroids) {
  for (agent in agents) {
    for (timepoint in timepoints) {
      tmp[[paste0(
        spheroid,
        "_",
        agent,
        "_",
        timepoint
      )]] <- all_diff_ex[[spheroid]][[agent]][[timepoint]] %>%
        rowData(.) %>%
        as_tibble(.) %>%
        select(
          Protein.Group,
          Protein.Names,
          Genes,
          logFC,
          adj.P.Val
        ) %>%
        arrange(adj.P.Val) %>%
        filter(adj.P.Val < pval) %>%
        filter(abs(logFC) > log_fc)
    }
  }
}

diff_ex_prots <- bind_rows(
  tmp,
  .id = "spheroid_agent_timepoint"
) %>%
  separate(
    spheroid_agent_timepoint,
    into = c("spheroid", "agent", "timepoint"),
    sep = "_"
  ) %>%
  select(
    spheroid,
    agent,
    timepoint,
    Protein.Group,
    Protein.Names,
    Genes,
    logFC,
    adj.P.Val
  )
```

To prepare the data for plotting, we will group the differentially expressed proteins by spheroid, agent, timepoint and direction (up or down), and count the number of differentially expressed proteins in each group. We will also complete the data frame to include all combinations of spheroid, agent, timepoint and direction, filling in any missing combinations with a count of 0. Finally, we will convert the direction and timepoint columns to factors with specified levels, and set the count of down-regulated proteins to be negative for plotting purposes.

```{r}
#| label: prep-diff-ex-prots-for-plotting
#| 
diff_ex_prots_grouped <- diff_ex_prots %>%
  mutate(
    direction = case_when(
      logFC > 0 ~ "up",
      logFC < 0 ~ "down",
      TRUE ~ "no_change"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(spheroid, agent, timepoint, direction) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  complete(spheroid, agent, timepoint, direction, fill = list(count = 0)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    direction = factor(direction, levels = c("up", "down", "no_change"))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    timepoint = factor(timepoint, levels = c("8hr", "24hr", "48hr"))
  ) %>%
  mutate(count = ifelse(direction == "down", -count, count))
```

### Differentially Expressed Proteins Count

First we will generate a bar plot showing the number of differentially expressed proteins for each spheroid, agent and timepoint, grouped by direction (up or down). We will use the `geom_col_pattern` function from the `ggpattern` package to create a bar plot with patterns for each spheroid, and colors for each agent. We will also use a pseudo-log scale for the y-axis to better visualize the counts of differentially expressed proteins.

Crucially, we will use the `facet_wrap` function to create separate panels for up-regulated and down-regulated proteins, allowing us to easily compare the number of differentially expressed proteins in each direction across spheroids, agents and timepoints, but won't be grouping (facetting) by spheroid.

```{r}
#| label: plot-diff-ex-prots-count
#| fig.height: 6
#| fig.width: 8
#| fig.align: "center"
#| fig.cap: "Differentially expressed proteins across spheroids, agents and timepoints."
#| 

plot_diff_ex_prots_count <- ggplot(
  diff_ex_prots_grouped,
  aes(x = timepoint, y = count, fill = agent)
) +
  geom_col_pattern(
    aes(pattern = spheroid),
    position = position_dodge2(preserve = "single"),
    color = "black",
    pattern_color = "black",
    pattern_fill = "black",
    # pattern_size = 0.5,
    pattern_angle = 45,
    pattern_density = 0.05,
    pattern_spacing = 0.02
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(trans = "pseudo_log") +
  guides(y = guide_axis_logticks(negative.small = 1)) +
  scale_pattern_manual(
    values = patterns,
    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(fill = "grey70")) # <- make lighter
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = agent_colors,
    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(pattern = "none")) # <- hide pattern
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~direction, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Differentially expressed proteins across spheroids, agents and timepoints",
    x = "Timepoint",
    y = "Count of differentially expressed proteins",
    fill = "Agent"
  )
print(plot_diff_ex_prots_count)
```

```{r}
  height = 6,
  width = 8
)
```

This will allow us to see how the number of differentially expressed proteins varies across spheroids, agents and timepoints, and also how it varies between up-regulated and down-regulated proteins.

Now we can generate the individual bar plots for each agent and timepoint, showing the top enriched pathways based on the adjusted p-value. We will store the plots in a list for later use where we will combine the plots for each spheroid and agent into a single plot. 

```{r}
#| label: pathway-enrichment-analysis

plots <- list()
for (spheroid in spheroids) {
  for (agent in agents) {
    for (timepoint in timepoints) {
      tryCatch(
        {
          enriched_pathways <- all_enriched_pathways[[spheroid]][[agent]][[
            timepoint
          ]]
          plot <- plot_leapr_bar(
            enriched_pathways,
            paste0(spheroid, ": ", agent, ' at ', timepoint),
            top_n = 5
          )
          plots[[spheroid]][[agent]][[timepoint]] <- plot
        },
        error = function(msg) {
          message(
            paste0(
              "pval of '",
              pval,
              "' did not result in differentially expressed proteins for agent '",
              agent,
              "' at timepoint '",
              timepoint,
              "'"
            )
          )
          return(NA)
        }
      )
    }
  }
}
```

Once the individual plots are generated, we can combine them into a single plot for each spheroid and agent, showing the top enriched pathways across all timepoints. We will use the `plot_layout` function from the `patchwork` package to arrange the individual plots in a grid layout.

After getting the overview of the enriched pathways across all spheroids, agents, and timepoints, we can see that one of the agents that shows the highest number of enriched pathways across spheroids is Mirda. We will now focus on the Mirda agent and generate a combined plot for all spheroids at the 48hr timepoint, which shows the top enriched pathways based on the adjusted p-value.

```{r}
#| label: combine-pathway-enrichment-mirda-plot

combine_plots <- function(plots, timepoint, agent) {
  spheroids <- names(plots)
  plot_combined <- plots[[spheroids[1]]][[agent]][[timepoint]]
  for (i in 2:length(spheroids)) {
    plot_combined <- plot_combined +
      plots[[spheroids[i]]][[agent]][[timepoint]]
  }
  plot_combined <- plot_combined +
    plot_layout(nrow = length(spheroids)) # +

  return(plot_combined)
}

combined_plots <- list()
combined_plots[["Mirda_48h"]] <- combine_plots(
  plots,
  timepoint = timepoints[3],
  agent = "Mirda"
)

combined_plots[["TNO155_48h"]] <- combine_plots(
  plots,
  timepoint = timepoints[3],
  agent = "TNO155"
)

for (plot in combined_plots) {
  print(plot)
}
```

And as always we will save the combined plot for Mirda at the 48hr timepoint across all spheroids to a file in the output directory.

## Heatmap of differentially expressed proteins in enriched pathways

Now that we have identified the differentially expressed proteins and the enriched pathways, we can generate a heatmap of the differentially expressed proteins in the enriched pathways.

Given the information that we have gathered so far, we will focus on the 48hr timepoint, as it has the most significantly enriched pathways and differentially expressed proteins. We will gather the differentially expressed proteins in the enriched pathways into a single data frame, and then generate a heatmap of the differentially expressed proteins in the enriched pathways.

```{r}
#| label: gather-diff-ex-prots-in-enriched-pathways
#| 
timepoint <- "48hr"

dfs <- list()
for (spheroid in spheroids) {
  for (agent in agents) {
    prot_data <- all_enriched_pathways[[spheroid]][[agent]][[timepoint]] %>%
      rownames_to_column(., var = "pathway") %>%
      as_tibble(.) %>%
      arrange(BH_pvalue) %>%
      filter(BH_pvalue < 0.05) %>%
      select(
        pathway,
        ingroupnames
      ) %>%
      separate_rows(ingroupnames, sep = ", ") %>%
      rename(., ingroupnames = "protein")
    dfs[[paste0(spheroid, "_", agent)]] <- prot_data
  }
}
prots_data <- bind_rows(dfs, .id = "spheroid_agent") %>%
  separate(spheroid_agent, into = c("spheroid", "agent"), sep = "_")

prots <- unique(prots_data$protein)

se_diff_ex_prots <- experiment[
  rowData(experiment)$Genes %in% prots,
  colData(experiment)$timepoint == "48hr"
]
```

With the data gathered we can generate a heatmap of the differentially expressed proteins in the enriched pathways. Below we define a helper function to generate the heatmap, which takes in a `SummarizedExperiment` object and returns a `pheatmap` object.

```{r}
#| label: plot-heatmap-helper-function
#| 
plot_heatmap <- function(
  se,
  title = "Differentially expressed proteins in enriched pathways"
) {
  annotations_col <- as.data.frame(colData(se)) %>%
    select(spheroid, agent) %>%
    mutate(
      spheroid = factor(
        spheroid,
        levels = unique(colData(se)$spheroid)
      ),
      agent = factor(agent, levels = unique(colData(se)$agent))
    )

  # setting the color scheme for the annotations
  annotation_colors <- list(
    agent = c(
      "DMSO" = color_vals_black_first[1],
      "Mirda" = color_vals_black_first[2],
      "Palbo" = color_vals_black_first[3],
      "TNO155" = color_vals_black_first[5],
      "Vorino" = color_vals_black_first[7]
    ),
    spheroid = if (eval_mn2) {
      c(
        "JHU2002" = "#E41A1C",
        "MN4" = "#377EB8",
        "WU225" = "#4DAF4A",
        "MN2" = "#984EA3"
      )
    } else {
      c(
        "JHU2002" = "#E41A1C",
        "MN4" = "#377EB8",
        "WU225" = "#4DAF4A"
      )
    }
  )

  # map gene names to rownames of the assay data
  data_mat <- assay(se)
  gl <- rowData(se)$Genes
  gl[duplicated(gl)] <- paste0(gl[duplicated(gl)], '-dupe')
  rownames(data_mat) <- gl

  # generate the actual plot using pheatmap
  p_heatmap <- pheatmap(
    data_mat,
    cluster_rows = TRUE,
    cluster_cols = TRUE,
    annotation_colors = annotation_colors,
    show_rownames = TRUE,
    show_colnames = FALSE,
    annotation_col = annotations_col,
    cutree_cols = if (eval_mn2) 4 else 3,
    main = title
  )

  return(p_heatmap)
}
```

Using the helper function defined above, we can generate the heatmap of the differentially expressed proteins in the enriched pathways.

This heatmap will give us a broad overview of the differentially expressed proteins in the enriched pathways across spheroids and agents at the 48hr timepoint, allowing us to identify any patterns or trends in the data.

```{r}
#| label: plot-diff-ex-prots-in-enriched-pathways-heatmap
#| fig.height: 12
#| fig.width: 8
#| fig.align: "center"
#| fig.cap: "Heatmap of differentially expressed proteins in enriched pathways across spheroids and agents at the 48hr timepoint."
#| 
p_heatmap <- plot_heatmap(se_diff_ex_prots)
print(p_heatmap)
```

```{r}
  height = 16,
  width = 8
)
```

```{r}
se_diff_ex_prots_per_pathway <- list()
pathways <- unique(sig_pathways$pathway)
timepoint <- "48hr"


for (pathway_name in pathways) {
  dfs <- list()
  for (spheroid in spheroids) {
    for (agent in agents) {
      prot_data <- all_enriched_pathways[[spheroid]][[agent]][[timepoint]] %>%
        rownames_to_column(., var = "pathway") %>%
        as_tibble(.) %>%
        arrange(BH_pvalue) %>%
        filter(BH_pvalue < 0.05) %>%
        select(
          pathway,
          ingroupnames
        ) %>%
        filter(pathway == pathway_name) %>%
        separate_rows(ingroupnames, sep = ", ") %>%
        rename(., ingroupnames = "protein")
      dfs[[paste0(spheroid, "_", agent)]] <- prot_data
    }
  }
  prots_data <- bind_rows(dfs, .id = "spheroid_agent") %>%
    separate(spheroid_agent, into = c("spheroid", "agent"), sep = "_")

  prots <- unique(prots_data$protein)

  se_diff_ex_prots_per_pathway[[pathway_name]] <- experiment[
    rowData(experiment)$Genes %in% prots,
    colData(experiment)$timepoint == "48hr"
  ]
}
```
